pill.desc: pale yellow, round, film-coated, biconvex tablet

tell: A 14-hour terminal half-life, and a meal that lifts exposure by up to 66%, set this integrase inhibitor apart.

clues.text: Food raises exposure, with meals increasing AUC by 33% to 66%. It is highly bound, at least 98.9%, to plasma protein, and feces carry 53% of the dose unchanged.
A sodium salt that is slightly soluble in water; the free acid has a molecular weight of 419.4.
Approved under an NDA as 10, 25 and 50 mg tablets, dosed once daily, with a dispersible tablet for oral suspension.
With no boxed warning, it is contraindicated after prior hypersensitivity and with dofetilide. Insomnia, fatigue and headache are the most common reactions.
HIV-1 infection in adults and pediatric patients weighing at least 2 kg, combined with other antiretrovirals, or with rilpivirine as a complete regimen.
An HIV integrase strand transfer inhibitor, an antiretroviral agent that acts against HIV-1.
The generic name begins with D and has twelve letters.
